articleTitle: Research on eigenvalues of TM modes in coaxial resonator with inner-outer corrugations
abstract: The coaxial cavity with inner-outer corrugations has been proven to have better mode selectivity. In this work the author study the TM modes in such cavity, some cases of the corrugation parameters are made to study the rearrangement of the eigenvalue spectrum. The comparison between the TE and TM modes are also made to help us to study them. The calculation of the eigenvalues is all based on the SHM method.

articleTitle: Re-examination of absolute instability near band edges in a traveling wave tube
abstract: We re-examine the beam mode and its interaction with the circuit mode in the immediate vicinity of the lower and upper band edges in a traveling wave tube (TWT). Contrary to previous findings, we show here that an absolute instability may arise, according the the Briggs-Bers criterion, at the lower band edge if the beam current is sufficiently high, even if the beam mode intersects with the circuit mode with a positive group velocity. However, the upper band edge was found to be more susceptible to absolute instability than the lower band edge, according to the threshold conditions that we derived analytically. Near the band edge, the Green's function shows possible transient growth in a TWT that is free of absolute instability.

articleTitle: Scandate cathode work function measurements at elevated temperature
abstract: The work function of a scandate cathode prepared using the L-S technique, and measured in vacuum at elevated temperature, is presented here. The scandate cathode had undergone emission testing and displayed excellent emission behavior in a close-spaced diode testing apparatus, before the work function measurements were carried out. The work function at room temperature was measured to be 4.81 eV, and this value tended to decrease as the temperature was raised to 800°C, with a minimum value existing at 600°C. The implications for this behavior are also discussed.

articleTitle: Folded waveguide traveling wave tube in a parallel configuration with a single electron beam
abstract: This work describes the design of a folded waveguide traveling wave tube (TWT) operating in G- band around 145 GHz. In order to achieve high output power and good linearity a new parallel approach, using a single electron beam, was used. The designed TWT showed a maximum saturation gain of 39 dB with a bandwidth of 8.3 GHz. The parallel configuration has better RF performances respect to a standard FWG-TWT without increasing the complexity of fabrication.

articleTitle: Medium power high efficiency Ka band
abstract: The paper shows a new generation high efficiency Ka- band TWT especially for high data rate signals which demands high output back-off operation. This TWT, named TL20075S, was not only designed for geostationary payloads but also for MEO orbits with electrical in orbit transfer (EOT). It is based on the well-known TL20073S Ka-band TWT. With this setup first time an average efficiency of more than 69% over 2.5GHz for saturation operation could be demonstrated. Simultaneously at 3 dB back-off operation with only half RF output power an average efficiency of more than 52%% over 2.5 GHz could be achieved. In this paper the new feasibilities of this efficiency improvement will be discussed. It could be used either for increased number of output channels, for significantly reduced thermal payload layout or for new ideas to omit a linearizer before the TWT for cost improvements. All together this design will give a high flexibility to the customer in his payload layout, as well as a changeability of orbit operation with flexible output power and flexible back-off adjustments. A broadband performance of 2.5 GHz extendable to 2.9GHz will give new standard Ka-band product for a wide operation usage.

articleTitle: Integrated waveguide assisted electron emission device
abstract: We introduce the novel approach along with the experimental demonstration of enhanced photon assisted electron emission from monolayer graphene sheet placed over an optical waveguide. A critical challenge on state of the art photon assisted electron emission is low quantum efficiency (QE). One technique that improves QE is enhancing the optical absorption of the incident laser. Here, we specifically introduce utilizing integrated photonic waveguide under electron emitter layer as a mean to transport the photons and evanescently couple them to emitter layer. This evanescent coupling occurs through longer interaction length and photons can be absorbed efficiently compared to free space laser illumination from top on a monolayer of graphene. We also measured the free space photon assisted electron emission from graphene sheet and compared with the performance of the integrated photon assisted emission device.

articleTitle: Synthesis of electron optics with convergent sheet beam at magnetically shielding cathode
abstract: The results of simulation of electron-optical systems with sheet electron beam with compression are presented. Electron gun is considered with thermionic and field emission cathodes with 2.1 0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The result of modeling the electron gun at linear compression of 14, the beam of current 0.1 A has dimension of 0.15 0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> are performed. The electric field on the cold cathode is 0.16· 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> V/cm at anode voltage 20000 V.

articleTitle: The sub-THz clinotron-multiplier
abstract: We outline an experimental set-up for the sub- terahertz CW clinotron (a BWO with a comb-type slow- wave structure and an inclined beam) frequency multiplier oscillator. The clinotron-multiplier operation is expected to quadruple f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> ~ 146.5 GHz (2.04 mm) microwave signal, which is generated in the buncher section of the device, to obtain f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> ~ 586 GHz (0.51 mm) signal in the catcher section. Some results of preliminary experimental tests with a prototype sub-THz clinotron-multiplier are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: M-type dispenser cathode accelerated life testing within a pierce gun configuration
abstract: Accelerated cathode life testing results are presented for M-type dispenser cathodes operating over the last two years. Emission activity curves have been taken for various cathode loadings up to 10.7 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">^</sup>2 on a monthly basis over the course of the experiment. Temperature limited to full space charge limited transition region knee temperature has been tracked over time. An attempt is made to predict end of life based on resultant trends.

articleTitle: Characterization of scandate cathode at different stages of processing
abstract: Characterization was performed on samples representing scandate cathodes at key stages of processing. This included the starting powders, sintered pellets, impregnated pellets and activated cathodes, with special emphasis on the impregnated state. It was observed that pores were occupied by scandia after the pressing and sintering stage, and were subsequently completely filled after the impregnation stage. Interestingly, streaks of scandium-containing phases were observed in the impregnated sample. Activated cathodes did not exhibit the expected morphology with highly faceted tungsten, which may be due to a high oxygen content that originated from the powder preparation process.

articleTitle: Slow-wave structures with the negative inductive coupling
abstract: The application of the negative inductive coupling in the periodic slow-wave structures makes it possible to flatten their dispersion characteristics without decreasing the interaction impedance. The provided in this paper demonstration of this effect on models of the impedance comb and the fingered comb confirm the possibility of the significant increase of the operating frequency band of the standard and fingered combs, the structures, which can be used in the high-power TWTs with the sheet electron beam.

articleTitle: The phase-space volume effect on the electron beam forming in the EOS of Ka-band devices with a high aspect ratio field-emission cathode
abstract: The research results of the feasibility of using field-emission cathode cells with glassy carbon emitters with large aspect ratio in microwave K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub>-band devices are presented. The phase-space volume effect on flow generated by the field emission cathode matrix on its transverse dimension in the channel is shown.

articleTitle: 3-D printed Ka-band sine waveguide slow-wave structures
abstract: 3-D printed Ka-band sine waveguide (SWG) slow wave structures (SWSs) are presented in this paper. A kinds of 3-D printing technologies, rapid investment casting (RIC) with brass, have been considered. The VSWR of the assembled 3-D printed brass SWG SWS is less than 1.37, and the dissipative attenuation ranges between 0.025 and 0.054 dB/mm at 33-40 GHz. The 3-D printing technologies appear as a promising fabrication method for vacuum electron devices fabrication with the advantages of low-cost and rapid-prototyping compared with traditional machining processes.

articleTitle: An investigation on the phase composition and the electron emission capacity of the aluminate impregnants for the dispenser cathodes
abstract: The phase components in the xBaO·CaO·2Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (where x varies from 5.0 to 6.0) system were investigated by using of the X-ray diffraction. The results illustrate that 5B·C·2A and 6B·C·2A compounds synthesized by co-precipitation are of single-phase with B5CA and B3CA structure after sintering at 1200 °С, respectively. Based on the Current-Voltage characteristics tests, the divergent current density J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">div</inf> is 7.2 A·cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> occurring at 1100 °С for the impregnated cathode with 6B·C·2A aluminate.

articleTitle: Optimization of resistive attenuator coating for TWT performance improvement
abstract: A resistive attenuator coating of suitable profile is provided on dielectric rods to support helical slow-wave structure in a TWT to prevent oscillations. Moreover, its profile value, length etc plays an important role in gain and average power of the TWT. In this paper, authors have presented effect of attenuator coating length with fixed tip loss value and vis-à-vis on the gain and average output power of a low gain TWT and its comparison with measured data.

articleTitle: Manufacturing and performance results of a 1.2 MW peak, 704 MHz multi-beam inductive output tube
abstract: A multi-beam inductive output tube (MB-IOT) is being developed that will produce over 1.2 MW peak power at 704 MHz with over 65% efficiency. This is a collaborative effort between Thales Electron Devices (TED) and Communications & Power Industries (CPI) to design and fabricate a new RF source for the European Spallation Source (ESS). Design features and test results will be presented.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of the high-order mode oscillation in an intense relativistic Klystron amplifier
abstract: Based on much simulation, a four-cavity Intense Relativistic Klystron Amplifier with a superior performance has been designed, built and tested. An output power of 2.22 GW corresponding to 27.4% efficiency and 61 dB gain has been obtained. Moreover, the high-order mode oscillation is suppressed effectively, and an output power of 1.95 GW corresponding to 26% efficiency and 62 dB gain has been obtained in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic performance of helix TWT with beam loaded
abstract: To make more accurate analysis of electromagnetic performance of Helix Traveling Wave Tube (HTWT), the beam- loading effect is considered by treating the electron beam as an anisotropic medium focusing with an infinite magnetic field. Using this method, together with the sheath-helix model, the dispersion, coupling impedance and characteristic impedance of HTWT are obtained and compared with those from cold-test simulation. The results show that the electron beam will affect the EM performance of HTWT to some extent, and considering the effect is helpful when designing high-performance TWTs.

articleTitle: Study of dangling U-shaped slot-line slow wave structure
abstract: A novel dangling slot-line Slow-Wave Structure (DSL-SWS) has been proposed and studied. The high frequency characteristics of them, including dispersion properties, and coupling impedances, have been investigated, which shows the DSL-SWS is broadband and the dangling slot-line traveling-wave tube (DSL-TWT) has a low voltage. The transmission structure has been designed and simulated, the reflection coefficient is less than -15dB over the frequency range from 28-39 GHz. The stimulation result predicts that the DSL-SWS is a potential choice of the Miniaturization low voltage Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) and Backward Wave Oscillator.

articleTitle: Design and cold test of a W-band coaxial staggered double-grating slow-wave structure
abstract: A cold test experiment for a coaxial staggered double-grating slow wave structure (SWS) is designed, simulated and tested in the paper. A broadband input and output coupler is designed to excite the TEM mode in the SWS. The coupler consists of power dividers with multi-stage stepped waveguides and a 4-waveguides combiner. The CST simulation results and the cold test results for the coupler and the slow wave structure are compared.

articleTitle: Rising sun magnetron with diffraction output
abstract: This article describes process of designing new type of magnetron, based on Magnetron with Diffraction Output (MDO). It consists of Rising Sun anode structure, has megawatt range of output power, and works on L-band frequencies. It is shown that modifying classic anode cavities to Rising Sun type- structure is possible and it provides better mode separation and more stable signal. Design process was supported by Particle-in-Cell simulations in CST Studio Suite [6].

articleTitle: Researching on the wideband elliptical-section TE01-TE11 mode converter
abstract: The TE01-TE11 mode converter can convert the output mode of gyrotrons(their outputs are TE0n one or more circular modes) into TE11, in high power microwave system. And TE11 could be transformed into linearly polarizedGaussian-likee HE11 mode which facilitatestransmission and emission. The conventional researching on circular sections TE01-TE11 mode converter has been widely used. However, it has disadvantages in long length and narrow bandwidth. In this paper, a novel type of wideband Ka-band elliptical cross-section serpentine TE01-TE11 waveguide mode converter is proposedbased on theiterativemethod. This novel mode converter achieved a relative bandwidth 21.97% when the convertingefficiency is over 90%, at center frequency 30.5G. The structure length is only 510mm, which has coaxial-parallel input and output ports with smoothaxial curvature distribution. This researching offers good solutions to the disadvantages of the circular section TE01-TE11mode converter mentioned above.

articleTitle: The correct determination of the equivalent parameters of slow-wave structures
abstract: The possibility of the correct replacement of a slow-wave structure with the equivalent line is demonstrated on the simplest slow-wave structure model, impedance comb. The offered method of the exact replacement allows determination of the applicable to the circuit theory equivalent parameters. It is shown that the real power flow and the conduction current in the impedance electrode unambiguously determine equivalent parameters of the slow-wave structures.

articleTitle: Approximate analytic solution for the magnetic field distribution in the annual MFS cells of microwave power tubes
abstract: The approximate analytical expression is found for the components of the magnetic field in the first cell of the magnetic focusing system (MFS).

articleTitle: Multi-color terahertz smith-purcell free-electron laser based on frequency mixing
abstract: We proposed a free-electron beam driving frequency mixer with two cascaded gratings to generate terahertz wave radiation. The initial steady-current free-electron beam is macro-bunched by interacting with the self-excited backward slow-wave on the first grating, and then is further micro-bunched at higher frequencies on the following second grating. The multi-bunched electron beam then generates a series of coherent terahertz Smith-Purcell radiation from the second grating. The radiation can be tuned from 0.7 THz to 1.8 THz by changing the beam energy. It is a promising broad-tunable and multicolor terahertz source.

articleTitle: Preliminary study of helix arranged coupling slots in coupled cavity structure
abstract: A novel coupled cavity structure with helix arranged coupling slots has been studied. The dispersion characteristic of this structure is compared with hughes type coupled cavity structure to figure out its characteristic of weak dispersion. An extended interaction oscillator based on this structure has been operated to verify the feasibility of this novel coupled cavity structure. 2.4kW output power has been achieved when the voltage is 30.5kV and the current is 0.5A. Further study is ongoing to combine the advantages of coupled cavity structure and helix structure.

articleTitle: Progress of G-band folded waveguide pulsed Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: As Terahertz technology developed, the research for G-band folded waveguide Traveling Wave Tube (FWTWT) require higher power and wider band. The design simulation and experiment on 0.22THz pulsed FWTWT was presented, including electronic-optical system, folded waveguide slow wave structure (FWSWS) and input/output windows system. By the measurement, the G-band pulsed FWTWT can reach over 10W output power with 5GHz -3dB bandwidth at 3% duty cycle. The maximum output power is about 16W in frequency 221.5GHz, the gain is 31.5dB.

articleTitle: Analysis of the dispersion characteristics of the photonic crystal in the generator with intense relativistic electron beam
abstract: We have investigated of the electrodynamic characteristics of a photonic crystal, which is a system of thin metal plates alternating in two dimensions or pins. In particular, we obtained the dispersion characteristics of the photonic crystal under consideration for a number of the first working modes, and their evolution was studied when the geometric parameters of the system were changed. We have numerically studied the processes of interaction of a beam with an electromagnetic field in a photonic crystal.

articleTitle: MAGIC simulation of microwave generation using an active metamaterial powered by an electron beam
abstract: We use the particle-in-cell simulation code MAGIC to model the MIT metamaterial loaded waveguide high power microwave source design and demonstrate coherent microwave generation at 2.4 GHz. In our model, the lens magnetic field to shape the emitted electron beam was separated from the solenoidal magnetic field so that we can control the two magnetic fields independently as in the experiment. In the model, we also introduce the beam collector as in the MIT experiment. The MAGIC simulation results agree well with the MIT CST simulation results for all magnetic fields. We also provide some explanations of possible reasons for the difference between the results of simulation and MIT experiment for certain values of the magnetic field.

articleTitle: High power microwave generation by Cherenkov-cyclotron instability in a metamaterial structure with negative group velocity
abstract: We present the experimental results of a high power microwave source with a metamaterial structure designed at 2.4 GHz. The structure is a waveguide loaded with two metamaterial plates consisting of complementary split ring resonators placed in the waveguide with reverse symmetry. Two backward wave modes can propagate in the waveguide and interact with an electron beam of up to 490 kV, 84 A. Full microsecond long output microwave pulses up to 2.9 MW were measured with an efficiency of 9% from the Cherenkov-cyclotron instability.

articleTitle: Simulating magnetrons with VSim
abstract: We present the visual configuration and design of an 8-cavity strapped magnetron using the VSim GUI interface. We perform cold-test analyses by exciting the device with a sinc pulse distributed current located in one of the cavities. Using the VSim data analyzers, we determine the resonant π- and 2π-mode frequencies at 0.4 GHz and 2.02 GHz, respectively. We also show the scalar and vector field patterns formed when the device operates in these normal modes.

articleTitle: MICHELLE post processing for large scale problems and HPC environments using ParaView with a custom GUI interface
abstract: We present new visualization tools for the recently developed High Performance Computing (HPC) capability for the MICHELLE code. New HPC support has been implemented in the code and its environment over the past two years in support of rapid device design and optimization. Central to this is the adoption of HPC tools and the porting of the code to HPC platforms, which allows for accurate, high-resolution, large-scale models and simulations of multiple beam devices, such as MBK guns and MB-IOTs. Visual analysis and post-processing of simulation results from such large-scale models is a computational challenge that requires advanced scientific visualization tools such as ParaView, which was chosen for our program due to its flexibility to plug-in customization. To enhance usability and efficiency for new and existing MICHELLE users, a GUI plug-in to ParaView with MICHELLE-specific tools has been developed using the Qt GUI toolkit and Python. Here we present a description of the Qt plug-in with example problems, and a review of some ParaView capabilities. Also presented is real-world benchmarking of HPC visualization performance using ParaView in client-server mode.

articleTitle: Optimization of group delay distortion for a Ka-band coupled-cavity TWT
abstract: The group delay of a high efficiency Ka-band Coupled-Cavity Traveling-Wave Tube has been simulated and optimized with Microwave Tube Simulation Suite (MTSS). By increasing the opening angle of the coupling slot and adjusting the periodic length of the coupled cavity, the group delay of the Ka-band CCTWT is successfully reduced to less than 1ns.

articleTitle: Quality & reliability managements during production process of space TWTA
abstract: Due to its advantages of wideband, high gain and high efficiency, space TWTA is widely used in the field of electronic countermeasure, radar, guidance and digital transmission as the final stage power amplifier of microwave power transmitter system. According to the goal of navigation system engineering, space TWTA is required to have the characteristics of high reliability and long life. At present, the domestic TWTA has a problem of low reliability due to a series of reasons. Therefore, quality and reliability management work during production process of space TWTA.

articleTitle: Performance estimate of a low-THz helical groove-guide TWT
abstract: The paper presents the basic design of a low- THz TWT consisting of a helically arranged groove-guide driven by a hollow beam. The beam interacts with the wave in a periodic sequence of gaps. The small signal gain is estimated and spurious mode excitation is investigated. First simulation results are shown.

articleTitle: Microwave gain in a recirculating planar crossed-field amplifier
abstract: The Recirculating Planar Crossed-Field Amplifier (RPCFA) has demonstrated gain of an injected ~20 kW RF signal. The RPCFA concept is adapted from the Recirculating Planar Magnetron (RPM) also developed at the University of Michigan. The device was designed in simulation using Ansys HFSS and verified using the particle-in-cell code, MAGIC. In preliminary experiments, the RPCFA has demonstrated zero-drive stability and produced peak output powers up to 0.3-0.4 MW. The gain is shown to increase with the applied magnetic field, and output power is typically limited to about 0.4 MW, apparently by RF breakdown within the RPCFA SWS. Analysis of the amplified signal shows high spectral purity, with minimal contamination from frequencies other than the 2.84 GHz injected RF signal.

articleTitle: Improvement design of K-band 2×2 channels integrated TWTs
abstract: The periodic permanent magnet (PPM) focusing system and the helix slow wave structure of K-band 2×2 channels integrated TWTs are improved. The magnetic saturation in pole piece is reduced and the problem of magnetic axis shift is solved by reducing the channel radius. The improved focusing system is predicted to achieve over 99% of electron transmission rate. The saturated output power of each channel in the integrated TWT is more than 100 W.

articleTitle: Lagrangian large signal model for double corrugated waveguide
abstract: A novel code based on non-linear Lagrangian formulation of beam wave interaction in traveling wave tubes is presented, modified for non-rotationally symmetric slow wave structures, such as the double corrugated waveguide. By including axial variations in the electric field along the period of the structure, as well as radial and angular variations and a model for the space charge forces in the double corrugated waveguide, a code capable of describing the behavior of the double corrugated waveguide is written.

articleTitle: Research of electrodynamic characteristics of a double-gap Klystron resonator with quasi-fractal microstrip elements
abstract: Electrodynamic characteristics of a double-gap klystron resonator with the inductive quasi- fractal microstrip elements on the suspended ceramic substrate have been investigated. The developed resonator can find application in micro vacuum klystron devices in one - and multi-frequency mode of operation.

articleTitle: Effects of beam tunnel on 220GHz rectangular beam folded Waveguide Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: A novel rectangular beam folded waveguide traveling wave tube (RBFWG-TWT) was proposed for higher output power. In this paper, effects of beam tunnel on transmission properties was studied to investigate the proper size to prevent electromagnetic wave leaking from the electron port. Then a RBFWG-TWT operating at 220GHz was simulated by the Particle-in-cell (PIC). To obtain the optimized aspect ratio of the electron beam and beam tunnel, influence of broad and narrow sides on output power was also simulated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Design of high power average gyro-TWT collector (2) - maximizing the collection area and improving the collection uniformity
abstract: When the dissipated power density is determined, the effective collecting area and the collection uniformity must be improved in order to increase the total power capacity of collector. Starting from the electron trajectories, the electron beam distribution function with different initial phases are discussed in this paper. After analyzing the dissipated beam distribution functions in different collector, the collecting density function can be derived. Finally, the effective collecting area and collection uniformity is improved by effectively designing collector profile and the magnetic field distribution.

articleTitle: Design of interaction cavity of a 263GHz gyrotron oscillator for DNP-NMR
abstract: The paper describes simulation and design of a 263GHz gyrotron oscillator operating in the circular TE03 mode at the fundamental cyclotron harmonic. A self- consistent nonlinear code and a particle-in-cell (PIC) software were used to investigate the beam-wave interaction. Results of PIC simulations show that the gyrotron oscillator can generate peak power of 460.2W at 263.13GHz when utilized a 10kV, 0.2A, v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">_</sub>/v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">||</sub> =3D2.0 electron beam from a magnetron injection gun, and the results of simulations show the gyrotron operates stably in the operating mode.

articleTitle: Design studies of a RF interaction cavity for a 4 MW, 170 GHz triangular corrugated coaxial cavity gyrotron
abstract: Gyrotrons are very powerful coherent sources of radiation. In coaxial cavity gyrotron, an insert is present in the cavity which leads to reduction in the voltage depression and change the eigenvalue, depending on the radii ratio. As a result a coaxial cavity can be fine- tuned for very higher power at very higher frequencies in comparison to cylindrical cavity. In this paper design studies of a coaxial cavity for 170 GHz, 4 MW gyrotron are given. The insert is corrugated with triangular corrugations. The advantage of such a corrugation type is that it allows more number of slots to be included on the insert, without causing the problem of localized heating. Single mode self consistent calculation is carried out for the calculation of output power and efficiency. Wall losses and diffractive quality factors for desired and competing modes have been calculated.

articleTitle: The dipole model at the atomic scale: Explaining variations in work function due to configurational and compositional changes in Ba/Sc/O adsorbates on W (001), (110), and (112)
abstract: The adsorption of alkaline-earth metals (and/or their oxides) on transition metal surfaces reduces the work function significantly, an effect that has been widely applied in thermionic dispenser cathodes to improve electron emission. Even slight changes in adsorbate composition and configuration on the emitting surface can lead to remarkable differences in work function. In this work, atomistic calculations of the structure, work function, and stability of a range of Ba/Sc/O-adsorbed W surfaces relevant to scandate cathodes are used to develop an atomic-scale understanding of the mechanisms leading to changes in work function. While a range of theoretical explanations have been put forward to explain how alkaline-earth ions or oxide layers modify the work function, the present results strongly support the idea that surface dipole effects are the critical mechanism controlling work function changes. These results provide significant insight into efforts to design new and novel low-work function surfaces and materials.

articleTitle: Design of ultra-thin dielectric waveguide meander line for 850GHz Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: We presented an ultra-thin optical waveguide which can be used as slow wave structure for Terahertz (THz) TWT in this paper. This ultra-thin optical waveguide has large dimensions, which can be fabricated by microelectronic fabrication processing. The simulation results show that when the height of waveguide less than 45μm, this waveguide has abnormal limitation of mode- filed, most of the confined power is transmitted in air, which can be used to interaction with electronic beam. Based on this, this waveguide can be designed as meander line slow wave structure (SWS). The dispersion and pierce impedance were simulated and the simulation results show that this structure is suitable for TWT design.

articleTitle: Improvements in scandate powder synthesis
abstract: We study the effect on emission and life of variations in: 1) tungsten oxidation; 2) scandia concentration; 3) sintering temperature; 4) tungsten particles size. Both L-L and L-S powders were studied. Over 32 powders were synthesized, over 100 cathodes were emission tested, 80 of which received life testing. Many were tested for mechanical strength. In addition, 115 SEM/EDS tests were performed on the surface and cross-sections of sintered cathode matrices.

articleTitle: Materials characterization of surface phases in scandate cathodes
abstract: Electron-transparent lamellae were extracted from a pair of scandate cathodes, each one made from L-S or L-L powders, and then examined using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). A distribution of chemically distinct phases appeared on the surface of tungsten grains, as well as inside them. While Ba and Al coexist in the same oxide particles, Sc exists separately in its own oxide phase. No evidence was found for the presence of a semiconducting layer containing both Ba and Sc, although it was specifically sought.

articleTitle: Experiments on a 140 GHz, TE22.6-mode gyrotron
abstract: A double-anode magnetron injection gun (MIG) has been designed and taken place of the single-anode magnetic injection gun used in the first version 140GHz gyrotron. The others parameters of a 140GHz TE22.6-mode gyrotron are same as the first version. And the second version gyrotron has been fabricated and tested. With pulse width 300-us and repetition frequency of 5 Hz, an output power of ~430kW with frequency of 140.2GHz is achieved in operating voltage 68kV, electron beam 28A, corresponding to 22.6% of efficiency.

articleTitle: Design studies of a magnetron injection gun for a 2MW, multi-frequency (220/251.5/283 GHz) triangular corrugated coaxial cavity gyrotron
abstract: In this paper, design studies of an electron gun supporting multi-frequency operation in an already proposed dual regime (220/251.5 GHz) coaxial cavity gyrotron is presented. For this third operating frequency of 283 GHz, the cavity mode is chosen as TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">62;38</sub>. Initial design studies of the magnetron injection gun are carried out through our in house code Gyrotron Design Suite version 4.1 (GDSv4.1 2016). Parametric optimization and simulation are carried out using the particle trajectory code ESRAY. These studies confirm that the electron gun designed for the dual regime operation of the coaxial cavity gyrotron can be used to support the third operating frequency of 283 GHz.

articleTitle: Solid-state grid modulator for power vacuum microwave devices
abstract: A solid-state pulsed modulator for grid controlled power microwave devices has been developed and experimental studied. An output stage of the modulator includes two special designed high-voltage switches on the basis of series connected MOSFETs. The tests carried out in the laboratories of the RPE "Toriy " have shown the stability of the modulator operation in the pulse duration range from 1 μs to 0.5 ms at amplitude voltages up to 10 kV.

articleTitle: Mapping conditions for the formation of high-performance scandate cathodes: New insights into the role of sc
abstract: TEM and SEM studies have shown that tungsten grains in low work function scandate cathodes are well-faceted and exhibit a characteristic shape consisting of (001), (110), and (112) surfaces. These surfaces appear with characteristic relative surface areas. The relative surface areas of facets expressed on a crystallite are controlled by the relative energies of each facet present. In turn, relative surface energies are controlled by the structure, composition, and chemical potential (equivalently, partial pressure) of species present in a cathode system- generally, in the case of scandate cathodes, Ba, Sc, O and W. Combining quantum mechanical calculations of the atomic structure and energy of Ba/Sc/O-adsorbed W facets with thermodynamic models of chemical potential dependent surface energies, we have screened a large number of possible surface configurations and chemical conditions to identify a small number of candidate structures and ranges of stability that are consistent with experimental observations. These results represent a map of chemical conditions necessary to yield experimentally observed cathode grain shapes, and suggest a role for Sc that explains both the superior thermionic emission properties of low work function scandate cathodes and manufacturing/reproducibility problems that have limited scandate cathode adoption by industry and the military.

articleTitle: A novel technique to model ultrafast electron microscope
abstract: This paper will present the continuation of the work begun last year to model ultrafast electron microscopes. A special feature of this type of microscopes is that only a single shot of electron bunch at extremely high spatial and temporal resolution is needed. A numerical technique using a virtual moving mesh to encapsulate the bunch was developed and implemented in Beam Optics Analyzer. The Poisson electric field due to space charge is solved only for the moving mesh; thus, can be at very high fidelity but requires much less computational resources. The method is found to be very efficient and accurate. The transverse emittance with thermal effects grows to less than 0.09 πμ.

articleTitle: Thermal-hydraulic design and analysis for high power gyro-TWT collector
abstract: For the sake of improving the power capability of collector, a helical groove collector is presented in this paper, which has a larger dissipation area than the island- structure collector and straight groove collector. So it is designed and investigated. And the maximum temperature decreases from 264 °С to 99 °С when mass-flow-inlet is 0.5kg/s and the density of spent electron beam is 0.5kW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Meanwhile, the phase change of coolant is also considered that has an ineffaceable influence on the results. The power capability of collector get improved 70%.

articleTitle: Prediction and measurement of return loss in helix output circuits
abstract: Return Loss in a Helix TWT output circuit vs. frequency is both physically measured and modeled using 3D RF simulation software. The modeled RF circuit extends from helix sever to output waveguide. Comparison of both sets of data show strongly correlated results both in phase and magnitude over a broad frequency range.

articleTitle: Development of the DBS band, 1,250 watt CW, air-cooled helix TWT
abstract: Communications and Power Industries (CPI) has developed the VTU-6398D9A, a compact, high Continuous Wave (CW) power, high efficiency and forced air-cooled helix vacuum electron device. The new product was developed in 2017 to serve the demanding Direct Broadcast Satellite (DBS) Satcom market. The helix Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) operates with a 1,100 MHz instantaneous bandwidth and covers the full extended DBS band of 17.3 to 18.4 GHz. The minimum CW RF output power is 1,250 watts. The small signal gain is typically 49 dB, and the total gain variation over the full extended band is typically less than 1.5 dB. High overall efficiency is obtained by using a robust two-stage depressed collector and selecting operating voltages that simultaneously increase efficiency, reduce prime power, and maintain low body/helix current. Prime power is typically 3,995 watts. Low internal operating temperatures are achieved by way of advanced forced air heat exchangers. The TWT has overall dimensions of 5 inches wide by 20 inches long by 6 inches tall and weighs less than 30pounds. The predicted and measured performance data are compared.

articleTitle: Design of a wide bandwidth dielectric loading directional coupler for gyro-TWT
abstract: In this paper, a cylindrical TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode to rectangular TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> mode directional coupler with dielectric loading has been designed and simulated based on the theory of small aperture coupling for the power measurement of gyro-TWT. The 32 coupling apertures and over-mode rectangular waveguide, applied in this design demonstrates great improvement on the bandwidth expansion and volume reduced. For the suppression of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> mode (the main high-order mode) excited in the slave over-mode rectangular waveguide, two pairs of striped absorption material is designed and optimized in HFSS. The coupling degree - 48 dB ± 0.2 dB and the directivity over 25dB within 14GHz bandwidth is obtained.

articleTitle: Back-off efficiency optimization of traveling-wave tubes using simulated annealing
abstract: A simulated annealing approach for delay line optimization is improved and extended to take modulated input signals in back-off operation into account. Envelope simulation in conjunction with CW electron energy distribu­tions are used for efficiency estimation. A Ku-Band helix traveling-wave tube is optimized and results are presented.

articleTitle: Gyrotrons on the cone-shaped waveguide
abstract: The results of calculations for a nonlinear model of a tunable frequency gyrotron on a cone-shaped waveguide and the main wave TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> are presented in the article. It is shown that the adjustment range can reach 2.8%. For the waveguide that is expanding along the axis, the "wave" efficiency of the device is 21% at the operating frequency of 10 GHz. To achieve these parameters it is necessary to divide the gyrotron electromagnet into two parts - the main electromagnet and auxiliary one, which must move along the length of the waveguide. At a frequency of200 GHz, the "wave " efficiency is reduced to 15%, while the ohmic losses in the walls of the waveguide are 3% of the power of the electron beam. For waveguide narrowing along the length of the waveguide, the "wave" efficiency can reach 29% at a frequency of 200 GHz, and the ohmic losses in the walls of the copper waveguide amount to 4% of the power of the electron beam.

articleTitle: Development of lab-prototype for 170 GHz short pulse gyrotron
abstract: This paper has been described capabilities towards design and development of 170 GHz, 100 KW (short pulse) demountable Gyrotron. Design and fabrication technologies for each and every component of 170 GHz Gyrotron have been developed. All components such as MIG, cavity, collector and RF window for high power 170 GHz Gyrotron with internal mode converter have been indigenously designed and developed at CSIR- CEERI. The integration and vacuum processing of complete demountable 170 GHz Gyrotron have been carried out. The overall length of the Gyrotron is around 2.2 meter and the weight is around 200 kg without cooling ducts.

articleTitle: Design and development of a 1,250 watt extended KU-band CW forced air-cooled Helix Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: Communication and Power Industries (CPI), USA has designed, and developed a 1,250 Watt forced air-cooled high power, high efficiency continuous wave Helix Traveling Wave tube, Model no. VTU6397J2 for Satcom applications. This paper presents the test results of the two initial prototypes produced and tested in an enhanced forced air-cooled cooling system. TWT design includes a coaxial SMA female input cable and WR-75 waveguide output connections. Both prototypes measured over 1,300 watts of average CW output power, over 51 dB of small signal gain across the extended Ku-band from 12.75 GHz through 14.80 GHz. Prototypes demonstrated excellent linearity and third-order intermodulation performances at 4 dB and 7 dB back-offs from rated output power (61.0 dBm). TWT design includes a standard electron Gun assembly with FE turn-on, an isolated anode, a two stage multi-stage depressed collector assembly, and a novel slow wave structure. Test results are in agreement with the design goals and customer specifications. The predicted and measured performance data are compared.

articleTitle: Molecular dynamics simulations of vacuum diodes
abstract: We describe the code used for high resolution molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of vacuum nanodiodes. The code includes full Coulomb interaction of electrons and offers several types of emission mechanisms with different geometries. It has been successfully used to study field emission and Child-Langmuir limited emissions.

articleTitle: The design and calculation of X-band broadband CW Klystron
abstract: The bandwidth of the high power klystron strongly depends on its output power level. Usually, the relative bandwidth is about 1~2% for X-band CW klystron with output power of several kilowatts. The relative bandwidth of 3~4% is required for some application for 5kW X-band CW klystron. In this paper, the design and calculation of the X-band klystron are presented. By optimizing the parameters of electron beam and RF interaction section, the relative bandwidth of 4%, efficiency of 25%, gain of 25dB have been obtained for 5kW X band CW klystron at beam voltage of 14kV and beam current of 1.66A. The influence of beam filling factor and radius of beam channel on the efficiency-frequency characteristics are described and discussed.

articleTitle: Study of instabilities in a double-staggered waveguide sheet beam TWT
abstract: The instabilities in a Ka-band double-staggered grating waveguide sheet beam TWT is studied in this paper based on CST particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation. The geometrical parameters are optimized to realize the broadband operation. Through the stability analysis of the slow wave structure (SWS), the regenerative oscillation is not only induced by outside port reflection produced by output and input coupler but also caused by inside refection (SWS).As for the outside reflection, it can be suppressed well by carefully design of the input and output coupler. An input signal with a continuous frequency sweep is employed in PIC simulation for studying this inside regenerative oscillation. At last, two methods for suppressing the oscillation have been put forward and proven effective.

articleTitle: Design collector for high average-power/CW gyro-devices (1) - methods of raising dissipated power density
abstract: There are two key issues to improve the collector dissipated power capacity: 1 ) Improving the dissipated power density; 2 ) Increasing effective collection area and collection uniformity. In this paper, the threshold factors of the dissipated power density determine are studied firstly, then the method about how to improve the dissipated power density under the condition of the stable working would be propose. Using this method the dissipated power density is increased to 1.65kw/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> while the tube works stably. By employing the electron collection smooth method (discuss in following papers), a total 200 kW dissipated power can be stably collected in a compact longitudinal collector. This collector is successfully applied in the Q-band high-average and continuous-wave gyrotron traveling wave tube to ensure a 10hours non-stop stable operation.

articleTitle: The research of excitation source in FDTD method for waveguide
abstract: Excitation source is an important part in finite difference time domain (FDTD) simulations. There are several kinds of excitation source, such as the hard field source, the transparent current source, the total field/scattered field (TF/SF) source, the transparent field source and so on. When simulating the waveguide, we need a transparent source to keep the exciting field at the source grids as desired in some cases, for example simulating the waveguide's discontinuities. In this paper, we proposed a new transparent field source without the auxiliary FDTD simulation, which can be more timesaving.

articleTitle: Investigation of Sc2 O3 contents for nano-sized Scandia doped dispenser cathode
abstract: Nano-sized Scandia Doped Dispenser cathode made from Scandia doped tungsten powder has been paid worldwide attention due to its high emission and satisfactory emission uniformity. Among the adopted doping techniques the liquid-liquid doping by Sol-Gel process is the most favorable for the performance of this kind of cathode. A further searching on the details of the processes is necessary for cathode manufacturing. In this study, Sc<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> contents of 1%wt., 3%wt., 5%wt. and 7%wt. (named Sc1, Sc3, Sc5 and Sc7) were added to the tungsten powder; their effects on microstructures and emission performance of the produced cathodes were investigated. The study proved that the nano-sized Sc<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> particles are getting richer from Sc1 to Sc7 but cover on the W grains in all cases. While there is a slight decrease in porosities from Sc1 to Sc7, the filled impregnant of Ba Ca aluminates for Sc1 to Sc5 is satisfied the requirement for dispenser cathode, but is obviously lower for Sc7. All cathodes made from Sc3, Sc5 and Sc7 reach a Space Charge Limited current density of about 50A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at true temperature of 960°C except Sc1 of 33A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The knee points at initial current density of 30A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> are 830C, 875°C and 920°C for Sc5, Sc3 and Sc7, respectively. Almost no knee can be observed for Sc1. Therefore, Sc5 and Sc3 exhibit the best emission and emission uniformity, Sc7 comes second and Sc1 goes the worst.

articleTitle: Multibeam electron-optical systems with curvilinear axis of the beam forming and transportation
abstract: The results of the calculation of a multibeam electron gun forming curvilinear electron beams are presented in this paper. The rotation of the electron beam is accomplished with the electrostatic fields of the electron lens, which is situated at an angle to the trajectory of the beam. The results of the calculation of the electron beam transportation in the magnetic fields of different configurations are also presented.

articleTitle: Engineering the field enhancement factor and work function toward ultra-low threshold field electron emitter
abstract: This paper presents the experimental demonstration of control over field enhancement factor and work function of the hybrid field emitter to reduce the threshold field required for electron emission. The field enhancement is engineered through microfabrication of the underlying silicon wafers, and the work function is controlled by the transfer and deposition of monolayer graphene and low work function lanthanum hexaboride (LaB<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>) nanoparticles. As a result, the threshold field, defined as the electric field required for 10 μA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of emission current density achieved as small as 2.6 V/μm. We also carry out photoemission spectroscopy (PES) to measure the effective work function of our emitters as 3.62eV, significantly lower than work function of the graphene. The measured work function allows us independent extraction of the field enhancement factor of underlying silicon tip array from Fowler-Nordheim (FN) analysis of the experimental I-E curves. Through these measurements and work function characterization, we show that the work function and field enhancement factor can be independently controlled, potentially enabling ultra-low turn on, uniform, and stable emitters.

articleTitle: The enhanced THz Smith-Purcell rradiation from the grating with holes
abstract: The mechanism of Smith-Purcell radiation can be explained with Huygens ' principle by the radiation of a moving oscillating dipole, which is formed by the moving charge and its image in the metallic grating. Here, an alternative way is presented to enhance the THz Smith-Purcell radiation. By drilling a hole in the fins of a grating as an effective electron channel, the oscillation dipole happens in two dimensions here, instead of one dimension. As a result, the Smith-Purcell radiation power is ten times more than the case in which the electron passes very close to the grating surface. This method is expected to improve the efficiency of the devices which are based on the Smith-Purcell radiation.

articleTitle: Emission micro-observation of dispenser cathode via DUV-PEEM/TEEM
abstract: In this paper, deep ultraviolet laser photo emission and thermal emission electron microscopy (DUV-PEEM/TEEM) with high resolution have been used to carry out research on M-type cathode and a new Sc- type impregnated dispenser cathode. The micro region photo emission electron images and thermal emission electron images of cathodes have been obtained. The results show that high emission regions of the new Sc-type impregnated dispenser cathode are almostly distributed on the edge of the particles and the tiny surface of a few tungsten particles, which have high intensity contrasted with the surrounding areas. For M-type cathode, the high emission regions are concentrated on the matrix pores, and it is not very uniform as we supposed.

articleTitle: Effects of Scandia distribution on surface structure of scandate cathodes
abstract: Scandate cathodes have long attracted attention due to their higher emission current density, apparent low work function, and anticipated improved longevity comparing to conventional cathodes. However, scandate cathodes have not been applied as extensively as their potential would imply, due to many unresolved issues, one of them being the non-uniformity of emission from the cathode surface. One possible reason for this, namely uneven distribution of scandia on tungsten, is investigated here. By comparing the initial microstructure of tungsten- scandia powder to resulting sintered pellets, we have discovered that more complete scandia coverage corresponds to a larger number of scandia particles distributed on sintered tungsten. Nearly all samples, when prepared as sintered pellets, exhibited a work function of 5.1 eV, as measured with a Kelvin probe.

articleTitle: Update on development of new generation of cathodes using additive manufacturing methods
abstract: In recent years, manufacturing of dispenser cathodes has become more challenging. Cathodes for new devices are smaller, dimensional and geometric tolerances are tighter, thermal and electric requirement are more demanding. At the same time, with advancement in scandate cathodes technology, it is clear that our traditional manufacturing techniques, based on decades old methods, may not be sufficient once this new technology is fully developed and scaled up to manufacturing. For that reason, we at Ceradyne Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of the 3M Company, are looking into alternative manufacturing methods to address these challenges.

articleTitle: Correlation between growth mechanism of macrocrystalline diamond-ultrananocrystalline diamond composite and mechanical properties of its thin THz TWT windows
abstract: Through engineering a multilayered structure of microcrystalhne diamond (MCD) and ultrananocrystalline diamond (UNCD), we have recently fabricated a 60 μm thick composite diamond film for THz TWT windows. Tests showed that such a composite diamond film possessed sufficient mechanical strength and air-tightness. The surface roughness of the composite was managed via structural design that the lapping and polishing process could be avoided. Correlation between Growth mechanism of MCD-UNCD composite and mechanical properties of its thin THz TWT windows is given and discussed.

articleTitle: Characterization of field emission from carbon nanotube fibers in varying cathode-anode gaps
abstract: This paper presents field emission (FE) from a single carbon nanotube (CNT) fiber with varying anode- cathode (AK) gap distances. We found that the field enhancement factor depends strongly on the finite AK gap distance, due to the combination of geometrical effects and possible fiber morphology change. The slope drop in the Fowler-Northeim (FN) plot of the FE data in the high voltage is related to the electrical contact resistance between the CNT fiber and the substrate.

articleTitle: MICHELLE simulation and performance using domain decomposition
abstract: Progress has been made in the area of domain decomposition using the NRL CAPSTONE mesher and the MICHELLE beam optics code. Domain decomposition, being the standard for parallelization for mesh-based solvers, has been implemented in the MICHELLE code environment. CAPSTONE was chosen as the volumetric mesher for a variety of reasons, but for this purpose it is suited to the production of Domain-Decomposed meshes. The approach taken to support domain-decomposition from the mesher through to the solution and visualization is presented.

articleTitle: Study on the beam-wave interaction in sine waveguide
abstract: A theoretical model for analyzing beam-wave interaction in sine waveguide (SWG) is proposed. The "hot" dispersion equation of the beam with arbitrary thickness is obtained by regarding the electron beam as a moving plasma dielectric. Moreover, the formula of gain growth rate is carried out.

articleTitle: Thermoelectron emission microscopy of Zr-coated scandate disperse cathode
abstract: A layer of Zr film about 30nm was deposited on the surface of impregnated scandate disperse cathode by PLD system. Thermoelectron Emission Microscope (TEEM) was used to characterize the influence of Zr film layer. The result shows that, the Zr film restrains emission of cathode to some degree. However, the uniformity of emission on cathode surface has been greatly improved.

articleTitle: Photonic crystal application for microwaves output induced by the beam-plasma instability in the absence of ions
abstract: In this paper we propose the application of photonic crystal structure for amplification of microwave oscillations in relativistic electron beam induced by the beam-plasma instability in the absence of ions. Previously, it has been shown that interaction between the electron beam and charged high-dense electron plasma represents a mechanism for microwaves generation in the range of 18-40 GHz depending on beam current and energy. From this point of viewpoint application of photonic crystal as an output electrodynamical structure seems to be a prospective way to gain the amplitude of longitudinal space-charge waves in the electron beam. So, this study aims at the model development and numerical particle-in-cell simulation of the described microwave system to consider its efficiency gain by means of photonic crystal.

articleTitle: Scaled experimental studies on radio frequency source for megawatt-class ionospheric heaters
abstract: Results of a scaled experiment using the electron beam produced by a gridded thermionic cathode from an Inductive Output Tube electron gun to drive an external lumped element circuit for high efficiency radio frequency generation are reported. The IOT gun produces an electron beam bunched at the driving frequency that is then collected by an external circuit for resonant impedance matching to the load. Results showed that effects such as the internal resistance of the inductor and deflection of beam electrons by the induced RF voltages on the beam collector are important considerations to be included in the design of a practical device using this configuration for high efficiency, MW-class RF sources for Mobile Ionospheric Heaters (MIHs).

articleTitle: A 100 kW 1.3 GHz phase locked magnetron for accelerators
abstract: Calabazas Creek Research, Inc., in collaboration with Fermilab and Communications & Power Industries, LLC, is developing a phase locked, 100 kW peak, 10 kW average 1.3 GHz magnetron-based RF system for driving accelerators. Phase locking will be achieved using an approach originated at Fermilab [1] that includes control of both amplitude and phase on a fast time scale. Experimental results, including demonstration of phase locking, are reported.

articleTitle: Regularities and mechanisms of development of instabilities in the system with intense relativistic electron beam
abstract: We have investigated analytically and numerically the development and interaction of Bursian/Pierce and diocotron instabilities in a relativistic electron beam propagating in a cylindrical drift chamber, depending on the beam geometry, current and the magnitude of the external uniform magnetic field. We have found out that the interaction of instabilities results in the formation of a virtual cathode with a complicated rotating helical (vortex) structure and several reflection regions (electron bunches) in the azimuthal direction. We have shown shown that the number of electron bunches in the azimuthal direction depends on the system parameters. We have discovered the connection between the number of bunches and the generation frequency.

articleTitle: Harmonic-frequency locking in planar magnetrons
abstract: The Multi-Frequency Recirculating Planar Magnetron is a crossed field microwave oscillator capable of generating high powers at two different frequencies. A novel locking phenomenon between the two oscillating structures in the MFRPM has been observed. A new magnetron, the Harmonic Recirculating Planar Magnetron (HRPM) is currently being designed to test the parameter space of this locking phenomenon.

articleTitle: Analysis of the test method for the helical waveguide dispersion characteristics of Ka band
abstract: This paper mainly analyzes two test methods of the characteristic of helical waveguide dispersion curve. Compared with the theoretical result, the errors obtained by resonance method and travelling wave method are less than 5%, this provides an effective method for the helical waveguide dispersion curve in practice.

articleTitle: Particle-in-cell simulation of a novel rectangular beam folded-waveguide traveling wave tube
abstract: To gain higher power, a novel rectangular beam folded waveguide traveling wave tube (RBFWG-TWT) was proposed in this paper. A 3-D CHIPIC code was introduced to analyze the amplification performance of RBFWG-TWT. The output power varying with voltage andfrequency was observed. The nonlinear phenomenon was simulated and analyzed in detail. It reveals that when the beam voltage and current are set to be 14.6 kV and 120 mA, respectively, the output power gain of RBFWG-TWT can reach 30.58dB, with a 3dB bandwidth of 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Narrowband THz generation by ultra-relativistic beam
abstract: High peak power, narrow band THz radiation can be generated by an ultrarelativistic electron beam passing through slow wave structure. In this paper we will review a series of recent experiments at Tsinghua University Accelerator Laboratory where a 31 MeV electron beam compressed to a sub-picosecond duration had been transported through dielectric loaded waveguide structures of various dimensions. Such high peak current electron beam generates wakefield, - a mix of TM0,N modes in the slow wave structure. This radiation is extracted from the slow wave structure and is characterized with interferometer. Narrowband signals in the range from 0.3 - 1.5 THz were measured with typical duration of few tens of picoseconds and few microjoules energy per pulse.

articleTitle: Effect of external electrical circuits on the operating conditions of high-power multiple-beam Klystron collectors
abstract: The paper deals with the effect of external electrical circuits on the static and dynamic conditions of high-power multiple-beam klystron collectors. It is shown that high-current systems may feature high-voltage breakdowns between the resonator unit and the collector that share the ground potential. A mathematical model describing the induced voltage on the collector of the O- type devices with allowance for external electrical circuits is presented. The possibility of suppressing the high-voltage breakdowns in the collector area due to external capacitive elements is theoretically and experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Dispersion characteristics of planar tape-helix using effective dielectric constant method
abstract: The dispersion characteristics of a planar tape-helix slow-wave structure (SWS) with straight-edge connections (PH-SEC) are evaluated by using effective dielectric constant (EDC) method. The EDC method helps to avoid the need to apply boundary conditions for straight-edge connections. The phase velocity obtained from the EDC-based analysis matches very well with that obtained from CST Microwave Studio for the frequency range far from cut-off. In the same frequency range, the dispersion characteristics obtained from the proposed analysis also match very well with the previously reported tape-helix analysis results of the PH-SEC.

articleTitle: THz electromagnetic radiation in beam-plasma system under different plasma distribution
abstract: Terahertz (THz) electromagnetic (EM) radiation in beam-plasma system under different plasma distribution has been simulated using particle-in-cell (PIC) method in this paper. The calculation results show that the electromagnetic radiation frequency under radially non-uniform plasma distribution is lower than that under uniform plasma distribution, which is good agreement with the theoretical analysis. The related physical analysis about the simulation results is given out. This work will give a better physical understanding of beam-plasma system and provide guidance to the project practice.

articleTitle: Relativistic magnetron with diffraction output (MDO) with a permanent magnet anode block configuration
abstract: This paper discusses the Magnetron with Diffraction Output (MDO) with transparent cathode and a permanent magnet configuration. Conventionally, to produce an axial magnetic field, a pulsed power system with Helmholtz coils is used. A permanent magnet configuration could be used as an alternative source of an axial magnetic field. The following substitution allows the MDO system to be independent of a pulsed power system for the magnetic field production, while maintaining high efficiency, and being compatible with repetition rate operation.

articleTitle: Investigation on a frequency tunable megawatt-class gyrotron at 0.24 THz
abstract: In this paper, we present an investigation and design on a frequency tunable megawatt-class gyrotron at 0.24 THz. The gyrotron can operate at frequencies from 234 GHz to 246 GHz in steps of 2.9 GHz, with operating modes TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">38.17</sub>, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">39.17</sub>, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40.17</sub>, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">41.17</sub>, and TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">42.17</sub>, respectively. In the analyses, the startup scenarios for operating modes were investigated by an in-house, developed, multi-mode, time-dependent code. The simulations result show that the output powers of 990 kW, 987 kW, 1060 kW, 1070 kW, and 1070 kW with corresponding interaction efficiencies of 36.5%, 36.8%, 39.3%, 39.5%, and 39.5% are achieved for operating modes TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">38.17</sub>, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">39.17</sub>, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40.17</sub>, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">41.17</sub>, and TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">42.17</sub>, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of a cascade high-power source with high efficiency
abstract: Cascade high-power microwave generator is an effective solution to provide a high level of miniaturization device. In this paper, we present a kind of novel cascade backward wave oscillator operating in the C band. The drift tube is employed to design a novel cascade backward wave oscillator. The phase synchronization of two output ports are analyzed by using Computer Simulation Technology (CST). Meanwhile, the CST Particle Studio (PS) is adopted to investigate the performance of the cascade backward oscillator. The Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation results show that the novel cascade backward oscillator is capable of achieving over 51.77% electronic efficiency from 4.8344 GHz to 4.8687GHz. Meanwhile, the maximum electronic efficiency can reach 82.44%% corresponding to a peak output power of 14 MW at 4.8466GHz.

articleTitle: Work function and stability of adsorbed Ba, O, and Ba-O species on an array of tungsten surfaces
abstract: In this work, we have used Density Functional Theory to explore the effect of O, Ba and Ba-O adsorbates on W surfaces to assess the impact of these adsorbates on the work function and surface stability for eight different W surface orientations. A discussion of the impact of different surface adsorbates on the surface stability and work function is presented, together with newly discovered stable Ba-O arrangements on the most stable W surfaces. Finally, we discuss the potential role of high index surfaces in electron emission, and the possible impact of W diffusion kinetics on the prevalence of high index surfaces.

articleTitle: Design of a 250 GHz disk-loaded waveguide TWT amplifier
abstract: A mm-wave disk-loaded waveguide (DLWG) traveling wave tube (TWT) amplifier is being designed for operation at 250 GHz. This design, in which coupling from cell to cell is via a highly ovesized beam tunnel, is attractive due to the ease in fabrication, even at high frequencies. The design has been conducted using analytic Pierce theory and time-domain simulations, which predict high gain. However, particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations show hybrid modes that de-bunch the electron beam and deteriorate the device performance when the structure length is increased to achieve very high gain. Additional design optimization is needed to avoid these unwanted modes.

articleTitle: Effect of pitch variation on the linearity of helix TWTs
abstract: The effect of variation in the pitches of different sections of a helix slow wave structure (SWS) on AM/PM and third order intermodulation distortion (C/3IM) is studied. A 2-section SWS operating in the frequency range, 10.5-12.3 GHz is considered. AM/PM curves at saturation are plotted and C/3IM values at saturation are tabulated for different pitch values.

articleTitle: Nano-sized Scandia doped dispenser cathode with annular shape for the hollow electron lenses for CERN high luminosity LHC project
abstract: The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is the world largest and most powerful accelerator for high energy physics. The High Luminosity LHC project (HL- LHC) foresees the construction and installation of important upgrades to increase the efficiency of the LHC machine. Hollow Electron Lenses (HEL) are one of the most promising methods being considered to control the beam halo and to improve the beam collimation system for HL-LHC. The source of the HEL is an annular shaped cathode which delivers a total current up to 5A. We developed a nano-sized Scandia doped dispenser cathode much smaller in size than the previously used B-type dispenser cathodes. The tests demonstrated that this cathode fulfils the specifications and can supply 5A full Space Charge Limited (SCL) current at a true temperature of about 850°C.

articleTitle: PIC simulation of a W-band gyro-TWT amplifier
abstract: A W-band gyrotron traveling tube(Gyro-TWT) amplifier has been studied using the particle-in-cell (PIC) code. To ensure stability, the ceramic loading technology is employed. The amplifier operates in the fundamental harmonic TE01 circular electric mode. The simulation predicts 117kw output power at W-band with 22.5% efficiency, 43dB gain and 5GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Recent progress of cathodes in high-power continuous wave magnetron tubes
abstract: In this paper we mainly describe the research progress in W base direct-heated cathode used in high power continuous wave tubes, which includes the Re-W cathode, ThO2-W cathode and the Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> W base cathode. The secondary electron emission yield of the Re-W cathode is reached 1.8 at room temperature. The lifetime of the ThO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-W cathode is beyond 6000 hours applied in 20kW continuous wave tube. The thermic emission density of the Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-Gd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> cathode is 3.7A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 1500 °Cbr.

articleTitle: Study on Ka-band broadband mode converter for gyro-TWT
abstract: A study of a Ka-band broadband mode converter for gyro-TWT has been presented. By using this mode converter, a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> cylindrical waveguide mode which is used as the operation mode for the gyro-TWT can be obtained from a TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> rectangular waveguide mode. The measurement result indicates that -3dB bandwidth of 6GHz has been obtained, which agrees well with the simulation results and doubles the level of the previous design. In addition, the influences of the critical dimensions on the transmission performance have also been analyzed. The mode converter is suitable for the broadband gyro-TWT.

articleTitle: Study of insertion loss for a Ka-band meander line slow-wave structure
abstract: Insertion loss of a V-shaped microstrip meander line slow-wave structure is studied based on actual fabrication and measurements at Ka-band. Empirical calculations and computer simulations are used to understand the high loss observed. The model of the microstrip line with triple-layer conductor, including adhesive layer, conductor layer and top protection layer, is built according to the fabrication process. The transmission characteristics are studied with different material components of the multilayer conductor. Simulation results show that the adhesive metal layer such as Ti can cause high loss because of relatively low conductivity and high current density. Some possible ways to reduce the loss have been suggested.

articleTitle: Analysis of faceted tungsten grains on the surfaces of scandate cathodes fabricated from L-S and L-L powders
abstract: Highly faceted tungsten grains were observed experimentally on the surfaces of two scandate cathodes that had been prepared from L-S and L-L powders. Using Wulff analysis, the facets were identified as {100}, {110} and {112} crystallographic planes, and the {112} facets dominated with respect to surface area. The effect of these facets on cathode emission properties is discussed in terms of their influence on work function and also values of the fitting parameter in the Richardson-Dushman equation J=3DAT<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>exp(-φ/kT).

articleTitle: Development of a pulsed TWTA EPC
abstract: Design and testing results of an Electronic Power Conditioners (EPC) working for pulsed space traveling wave tube amplifier are introduced in this paper. This EPC adopts 42V unsteady bus voltage and outputs helix voltage up to 8kV, which can handle peak output power of more than 1100W (pulse width 25μs) and average output power of more than 170W. The working temperature ranges from -35 °С to +75 °С, and the efficiency attained under full-load conditions was over 89%.By modular design, the filament voltage, the positive grid voltage and the helix voltage can be adjustable independently in a certain range (5%-10%). The control and protection circuit of the EPC uses anti-fuse FPGA and adopts Triple Module Redundancy technique to increase resistance to SEU effects in radiation environment. The robustness of the design was verified through strict qualification tests.

Author Keywords: pulsed space traveling wave tube amplifier

articleTitle: Design and test of a W-band photonic bandgap extended interaction Klystron amplifier
abstract: This report summarizes the progress of experimental efforts for the development a 94 GHz extended interaction klystron (EIK) with a photonic bandgap (PBG) based interaction structure. Input return loss measurements of the interaction structure are presented, demonstrating the successful fabrication of the input and output cavities of the EIK. Additionally, input return loss and insertion loss measurements of microwave-vacuum feedthrough windows are also presented. Finally, a review of the complete W-band experimental apparatus is given. Hot test experimental efforts for this study are expected to be completed by the 2018IVEC meeting.
